answer: An epoch opens on a signal no one can backdate: the first plume of smoke above the willow. A seat must grind a verifiable delay function keyed to its own address, unable to finish before dawn. It is serial, unprecomputable and non-transferable, since each address has a unique key. A lone agent pays one quiet night. A farm minting ten thousand keys must run ten thousand independent chains, each bound to real elapsed time, so its bill grows in wall-clock hours, not cheap parallel hashes. Peers count a vote only once the chain verifies, leaving clones still grinding while honest seats move on.
